title: Lumen Run
brief: Original-IP platformer game (sub-genre: 2d-platformer). Capture the core mechanics and game-feel of "Super Mario Bros. Wonder" (critically acclaimed, 92%) — but with your OWN original name, theme, characters and art. Do NOT reference or reuse that title's IP. SIGNATURE MECHANIC for this genre: gravity + jump/coyote/dash feel + hazard traversal + goal. MUST SHIP COMPLETE: a working menu (title + difficulty + how-to + settings via FFG.Shell), the page control bar (fullscreen/mute/pause), a clear win AND lose state, readable HUD, and polished feel — it must play start-to-finish with no manual fixes.

M2.done_when: every verb in the design doc implemented and survives the play-bot
M2.plan: Mechanics complete: wall-slide, coyote-time tuning, crumbling platforms, light-switch gates, checkpoint system, dash meter UI, all 3 hazard types functional.

M3.plan: Content complete: 5 levels designed and playable end-to-end, difficulty ramps correctly, menu shell (title/difficulty/how-to/settings) wired, win/lose screens with retry flow.

M4.plan: Polish pass: particle FX on dash/landing, ambient glow shaders, SFX placeholders (jump/dash/collect/death/goal), responsive page controls (fullscreen/mute/pause), level timer display, smooth camera follow.

M5.plan: Ship-ready: all Definition of Done criteria met, FFG.Shell integration verified, one full playthrough with no crashes or soft-locks, HUD readable at 1920x1080 and 1280x720, win/lose states trigger correctly every time.

design_doc.title: Lumen Run
design_doc.core_loop: Guide Lux, a nimble firefly explorer, through luminous caverns by running, jumping with coyote-time forgiveness, and dashing through the air to traverse collapsing platforms, light-activated hazards, and darkness zones. Each level ends at a Sacred Lantern goal; touching hazards or falling into darkness pits causes instant loss. Collect glow-orbs to power up your dash meter and unlock optional challenge paths. Smooth momentum-based movement rewards rhythm and timing over pixel-perfect execution.
design_doc.scope: IN: 5 levels (tutorial cave + 4 biome stages), menu shell (title/difficulty select/how-to-play/settings), win screen (level complete + time/orbs), lose screen (retry/quit), HUD (orb count, dash meter, timer), 3 hazard types (spikes, darkness pits, moving thorns), 2 platform types (solid, crumbling), light-switch puzzle gates, checkpoints mid-level. OUT: boss fights, multiplayer, cutscenes, dialogue, unlockable characters, procedural generation, save slots (single session play), leaderboards.
design_doc.art_direction: Palette: deep indigo/midnight blue backgrounds with vibrant cyan/lime/gold accents for interactive elements. Lux glows warm amber. Hazards glow red/crimson. Mood: bioluminescent underground wonderâ€”serene but tense. Particle trails on dash, soft bloom on light sources, simple geometric shapes with hand-drawn edge texture. Minimal UI with neon outlines.

definition_of_done: Player can launch game, see title screen, select difficulty (easy/normal/hard adjusts hazard speed), read how-to-play screen, adjust settings (volume/fullscreen).
Player can complete all 5 levels in sequence with clear progression feedback.
Win state: touching goal lantern shows win screen with time, orb count, retry/next level/quit buttons.
Lose state: touching hazard or falling into darkness shows lose screen with retry/quit buttons.
HUD displays orb count, dash meter, and timer at all times during gameplay.
Page controls (fullscreen toggle, mute toggle, pause menu) are visible and functional.
Jump has coyote-time (6 frames) and dash has clear visual feedback (particle trail).
Checkpoints restore player to last checkpoint on death, not level start.
No manual code edits required to playâ€”ships as single HTML bundle via FFG pipeline.
Game plays start-to-finish with no soft-locks, crashes, or missing assets.
